subject.title: Memory MVP: add review, edit, forget, and conflict-resolution flows

question: Should the memory lifecycle MVP be implemented in memory-core as the canonical default memory model, in memory-wiki as knowledge curation, or behind a new memory plugin API contract first?
rationale: The request defines persistent status semantics, audit/privacy behavior, plugin boundaries, and operator UX, so automation cannot choose the permanent product/API owner safely.

options.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
options.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict-resolution flows.

options.title: Route through memory-wiki
options.body: Treat the work as provenance-rich knowledge curation and extend memory-wiki claim, lint, and apply flows instead of changing active memory records now.

options.title: Define plugin API seams first
options.body: Add a memory lifecycle SDK contract so bundled and external memory plugins can implement the flows consistently before a default implementation lands.

recommendation.title: Design memory-core lifecycle MVP first
recommendation.body: Make memory-core own the v1 typed lifecycle schema and expose narrow review, edit, tombstone/forget, supersede, and conflict-resolution flows.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent memory schema and memory-wiki history makes this the strongest available routing candidate for the product/API choice.
